new_entities.name: Acne vulgaris
new_entities.description: Inflammatory and comedonal acne vulgaris of mild-to-moderate severity.

edges.effect_quant: Combined oral contraceptives reliably improve facial acne in women, with placebo-controlled trials showing fewer lesions and better global clearance ratings over time.
edges.population: adolescent and adult women using combined oral contraceptives for acne treatment
edges.mechanism: Combined oral contraceptives lower free-androgen signaling and reduce sebaceous drive, which directly targets one of the core hormonal pathways that worsens acne in many women. That makes the benefit more mechanistically coherent than a generic anti-inflammatory effect.
edges.summary: This edge is sturdier than many people realize. The Cochrane review of randomized trials showed that multiple combined oral contraceptives outperform placebo for acne, and later comparative meta-analysis suggested they can close much of the gap with oral antibiotics by six months.
edges.caveats: This is a women-specific treatment edge, not a universal acne intervention. Different formulations do not all perform identically, and contraceptive risks and preferences matter when translating efficacy into actual treatment choice.

evidence.citation: Arowojolu AO et al 2012 Cochrane Database Syst Rev
evidence.notes: Combined oral contraceptive pills for treatment of acne.

effect_quant.comparator: clear or almost clear skin with drospirenone-containing combined oral contraceptives versus placebo

evidence.citation: Koo EB et al 2014 J Am Acad Dermatol
evidence.notes: Meta-analysis comparing efficacy of antibiotics versus oral contraceptives in acne vulgaris.

evidence.citation: Daly CH et al 2022 Br J Dermatol
